chunks: From him, from al-Qāsim, from Abān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbd Allāh, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man whom the urine of beasts reaches: should he wash it or not? He said, “He washes the urine of the horse, the mule, and the donkey; and he sprinkles water over the urine of the camel and the sheep. And everything whose meat is eaten, there is no harm in its urine.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What these two reports contain of the command to wash the urine of donkeys and riding animals is to be understood as recommendation, in light of the reports we have mentioned earlier; and what further clarifies that is what he narrated:

key_terms.أَبْوَالُ الْبَهَائِمِ: the urine of livestock or beasts
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal ruling
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِبَوْلِهِ: there is no harm in its urine
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; indicating cleansing by washing
key_terms.يَنْضِحُ: he sprinkles water; a lighter form of purification
key_terms.يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ: whose meat is lawful to eat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal urine in Shia fiqh, and which kinds require washing?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on urine from different animals and distinguishes between cases requiring washing and cases where sprinkling water suffices. It is a jurisprudential report on ritual purity, and the compiler notes that the command to wash the urine of certain animals is to be understood as recommended rather than obligatory.
